_doc: SPEC §7.5 EXCLUSION-SCOPED CAMPAIGN. Each entry names one property the
sharded union==S campaign does NOT attempt. The campaign's claim is thereby
narrowed: equality holds over the corpus MINUS these properties, and the
full-corpus guarantee is NOT established while this list is non-empty.
THE LIST IS EMPTY, SO THIS IS THE ORDINARY FULL-CORPUS CAMPAIGN. §7.5 says so
explicitly: with E empty the section is unchanged and every property is
attempted exactly once. The machinery stays because the rule stays, and because
an empty list is a state a reader must be able to SEE — delete the artefact and
nothing says the campaign covers everything.
WHY gh-counts prop 1 IS NO LONGER EXCLUDED. It was excluded on a PROJECTION of
~647 minutes against a 330-minute step ceiling. The artefact's own return
condition said to test that before keeping it, and the test was run: shard 140
alone, under the campaign's OWN per-attempt wall cap (OATHRS_Z3_WALL_CAP_MS
3600000, not the 600000 default), finished in 218 MINUTES and recorded the
property `unproven` — a real verdict matching what S records, not an abort.
The projection had extrapolated from two runs that were CUT at 283/284 minutes
without ever finishing it, and the dedup landed in 37c074a had since taken this
property from 20 attempts to 15.
A FIRST ATTEMPT AT THIS TEST WAS WRONG AND IS RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REPEATED:
it ran with the DEFAULT 600000ms wall cap, finished in 100 minutes, and the
property ABORTED. That measured a configuration six times more aggressive than
the campaign's and cannot speak to it. `codex review` caught it before the
exclusion was removed on that basis.
ONE DIFFERENCE FROM THE CAMPAIGN REMAINS, STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. The test
ran at OATHRS_Z3_MEMORY_MB=3000; the CI worker sets 6000. That is the local
machine's mandated cap, and 3000 is TIGHTER than 6000 — so a memout is NOT the
untested direction, and completing under the tighter cap is the harder case.
What is genuinely untested is the OPPOSITE: with more memory z3 may explore
further on an attempt it would otherwise abandon, so the shard could take
LONGER in CI than the 218 minutes measured here, against a 330-minute step
ceiling. Even then the campaign is not wrong, only slower or failed: the
property is NOT in S, and an abort on a non-member is not a mismatch (merge
adjudication, oathrs/src/prove.rs). The dispatch is therefore the real test of
the remaining 112 minutes of headroom, and a shard-140 timeout is the signal to
restore this entry.
